title: Leave the Secrets Ashore
story:
RADIO, 11:58. Rafael Duarte, wind in the microphone.

"Engineer, the mainland lab pulls whatever image you hand me, and they scan it. Last time they found a credentials file inside and sent it straight back. Slow link, no second chances."

The `/workspace` folder holds the outbound report, a `secrets.env` full of credentials, and a 40 MB `raw/` folder of ice-dump data. The provided Dockerfile copies the whole folder with `COPY . /app`. Build `kestrel/outbound:1.0` from it so the report goes out and neither `secrets.env` nor `raw/` does. Do not change the Dockerfile.
objectives: Build the existing Dockerfile as `kestrel/outbound:1.0` (the image must be under 20 MB)
The image must contain `report.txt` but neither `secrets.env` nor `raw`
hints: `COPY .` sends everything in the build context into the image. A file named `.dockerignore` next to the Dockerfile tells Docker what to leave out of the context entirely.
`.dockerignore` lists one pattern per line, like a `.gitignore`. Name the credentials file and the data folder, then rebuild with `docker build -t NAME:TAG .`.

```bash
printf 'secrets.env\nraw\n' > .dockerignore
docker build -t kestrel/outbound:1.0 .
docker run --rm kestrel/outbound:1.0 ls /app
```

files.content: Kestrel Point weekly report: ice cores logged 14, generators nominal, morale cautious.

validation.description: The image contains `report.txt` but no `secrets.env` and no `raw` folder

debrief: `.dockerignore` filters the build context before anything is sent to the builder, so excluded files cannot leak into any layer and builds get faster. Pro tip: ignore `.git`, `*.env` and bulk data by default in every project.
